ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Psychology and Philosophy of Science This course is designed to address questions such as: Is Psychology a science? What is a scientific theory? What do scientists do when data goes against their theory? What does it mean to say a scientific theory explains the data? Can children learning about the natural world be thought of as "little scientists"? Is there a special form of reasoning used in science? What was the "cognitive revolution" (against Behaviorism) all about? Does the study of conscious phenomena (e.g., mental images) mean that Psychology is fundamentally different from sciences such as Chemistry and Physics? Will all of Psychology eventually be reduced to neuroscience? How can one distinguish pseudoscience from science? This course will help you see the "big picture" in field of Psychology. It will help you see the connections across areas in psychology and across the individual courses you have taken. It will show how evidence from Cognitive Psychology can be used to answer questions about the nature of science.
